title: Comparison return run
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, let $r$ be a register, and let $j_{RB}(b),j_{I1}(b),j_{I2}(b)$ be states for each Boolean $b$, with designated states $yes$ and $no$. Suppose that the ordinary transitions at these states perform, respectively, the specified return action, a one-cell left move, and the specified register-clearing action into $yes$ when $b$ is true and into $no$ otherwise; suppose none of these states is a call state. Let $c$ be a configuration whose register $r$ stores the word $w_r$ from cell $0$. For any $b$, input-head position $ip$, and integer $k$ with $0\le k\le |w_r|$, there is a time $T$ such that the run beginning in state $j_{RB}(b)$ with input-head position $ip$ and register-head position $k-1$ reaches state $yes$ if $b$ is true and $no$ otherwise, at input position $1$ and register-head position $0$. At every earlier time $t<T$, it is in some state $s$ that is not a call state, with register-head position $q$ satisfying $-1\le q\le |w_r|$.
hypotheses_covered: These states are not call states
